lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: What does your Reverence mean? What’s the trouble?

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: That’s why so many calamities come!

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: The ruling powers support heretics against the ministers of God!

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: What do you mean?

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: What do I mean? I’ll tell you what I mean.

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: I, yes I, mean to say that when a priest throws out of his cemetery the corpse of a heretic, no one, not even the King himself, has any right to interfere and much less to impose any punishment

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: But a little General—a little General Calamity—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: Padre, his Excellency is the Vice-Regal Patron!

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: Excellency! Vice-Regal Patron! What of that!

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: In other times he would have been dragged down a staircase as the religious orders once did with the impious Governor Bustamente.

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: Those were indeed the days of faith.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: I warn you that I can’t permit this! His Excellency represents his Majesty the King!

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: King or rook! What difference does that make?

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: For us there is no king other than the legitimate—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: Halt!

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: Either you withdraw what you have said or tomorrow I will report it to his Excellency!

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: Go ahead—right now—go on!

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: Do you think that because I wear the cloth, I’m afraid?

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: Go now, while I can lend you my carriage!

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: Gentlemen, you must not confuse things or seek for offenses where there are none.

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: We must distinguish in the words of Fray Damaso those of the man from those of the priest.

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: The latter, as such, per se, can never give offense, because they spring from absolute truth, while in those of the man there is a secondary distinction to be made:

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: those which he utters ab irato, those which he utters ex ore, but not in corde, and those which he does utter in corde.

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: These last are the only ones that can really offend, and only according to whether they preexisted as a motive in mente, or arose solely per accidens in the heat of the discussion, if there really exist—

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: But I, by accidens and for my own part, understand his motives, Padre Sibyla.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: I understand the motives about which your Reverence is going to make distinctions.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: During the absence of Padre Damaso from San Diego, his coadjutor buried the body of an extremely worthy individual

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: —yes, sir, extremely worthy, for I had had dealings with him many times and had been entertained in his house.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: What if he never went to confession, what does that matter?

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: Neither do I go to confession! But to say that he committed suicide is a lie, a slander!

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: A man such as he was, who has a son upon whom he centers his affection and hopes, a man who has faith in God, who recognizes his duties to society, a just and honorable man, does not commit suicide.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: This much I will say and will refrain from expressing the rest of my thoughts here, so please your Reverence.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: Now then, this priest on his return to the town, after maltreating the poor coadjutor, had the corpse dug up and taken away from the cemetery to be buried I don’t know where.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: The people of San Diego were cowardly enough not to protest, although it is true that few knew of the outrage.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: The dead man had no relatives there and his only son was in Europe.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: But his Excellency learned of the affair and as he is an upright man asked for some punishment

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: —and Padre Damaso was transferred to a better town.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Guevara
lines.text: That’s all there is to it. Now your Reverence can make your distinctions.

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: I’m sorry that I inadvertently brought up so delicate a subject.

lines.speaker: Fray Sibyla
lines.text: But, after all, if there has been a gain in the change of towns—

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: How is there to be a gain?

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: And what of all the things that are lost in moving, the letters, and the—

lines.speaker: Fray Damaso
lines.text: and everything that is mislaid?
